fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Walkway
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Multiple Structures; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and equipment so responding units can reach both structures without obstruction.
• Mark or post visible signage identifying the detached structures so responders can quickly distinguish them from the main residence during an incident.
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and allow emergency vehicles to pass without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation growing close to the structures to keep a clear path around exterior walls for responders working on foot.
• Install a secondary access point or gate at the rear of the property to reduce reliance on the single front access drive for responder movement.
• Keep any gates or barriers on the property unlocked or equipped with a Knox-style lockbox so responders can reach the rear without delay.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Along Driveway; Tree Cluster; Open Terrain; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin the tree cluster closest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim lower branches on large trees near the structure so branches do not extend close to the roofline or walls.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly against the exterior walls of the structure.
• Thin scattered shrubs and mixed vegetation on the sides of the structure to open up visible space around the building.
• Trim overhanging branches and cut back shrubs along the driveway so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep the driveway clear of fallen branches and debris that could slow vehicle movement during an evacuation.
• Clear vegetation at the rear of the property to allow better movement and visibility around the back of the structure.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is visible to emergency vehicles approaching from the main road.
